item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 272305
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores.

Central Subtropical Atlantic (AL91):
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles
east-northeast of Bermuda is moving quickly northeastward. This
system is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms, and it
could become a tropical depression in the next couple of days when
it turns eastward and slows down over the central Atlantic.
Environmental conditions are expected to become unfavorable for
development late this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Public Advisory Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 280234
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026
 
...FAY HOLDING ON AS A TROPICAL CYCLONE FOR NOW...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM GMT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...28.5N 43.8W
ABOUT 1170 MI...1880 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...30 MPH...45 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...S OR 190 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1012 MB...29.89 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM GMT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 28.5 North, longitude 43.8 West. The
depression is moving toward the south near 6 mph (9 km/h). A
south-southwest to southwest motion is expected over the next couple
of days, followed by a turn toward the west-southwest with an
increase in forward speed by mid-week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 30 mph (45 km/h) with higher gusts.
Fay will likely become a remnant low in a day or two, and
dissipate later in the week.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1012 mb (29.89 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 280236
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Mon Sep 28 2026
 
Little can be said about Fay that hasn't been said already across 
previous advisories. The storm continues to undergo rounds of 
diurnal, pulsating convection, allowing for it to remain a tropical 
depression despite being disorganized and weak. Scatterometry data 
from around 2300 UTC also confirms that a closed, albeit weak, 
circulation persists. With max winds from this scatterometry pass 
reading around 20 kt, the initial intensity for Fay was set at 25 
kt.
 
The initial motion was set at 190/5 kt. Fay is beginning to pick up 
speed as it escapes the influence of the subtropical Atlantic high 
and is carried more by the prevailing easterlies. A brief 
southeastward shift was evident on satellite just a few hours ago, 
but now Fay is beginning its forecasted southwestward to 
west-southwestward turn. The only notable change in the latest 
track forecast was to increase Fay's forward speed during the 
latter half of the forecast period, to fall better in line with the
HCCA guidance.

Global models continue to suggest that Fay will degenerate into 
a trough during the middle of the week, with post-tropical 
transition occuring just before. Fluctuations in Fay's intensity 
are expected so long as these diurnal cycles of convection 
continue, however with now two consecutive scatterometry passes 
depicting Fay's max winds at around 21 kt, the intensity forecast 
was left at 25 kt throughout the period, with little in the 
guidance and synoptic environment to suggest that Fay will 
strengthen meaningfully beyond that before finally dissipating.
